summaries.summary: COVID-19 affected more than one million individuals and caused more than 55,000 deaths as of April 3 in 2020, while population bias creates conflicting radiological findings conclusions.

The authors aim to use natural language processing on the CORD-19 dataset, containing over 45,000 scholarly articles including over 33,000 with full text, to discover COVID-19-related clinical findings.
The major contributions of this paper include:
The authors develop natural language processing methods to perform unbiased study of the correlation between radiological findings and COVID-19.
The authors develop a bootstrapping approach to train a sentence classifier with light-weight manual annotation effort for extracting radiological findings from literature.
Experiments verify the method, and from the CORD-19 dataset it successfully discovers clinical findings closely related with COVID-19.
Section 2 introduces the data, Section 3 presents the method, Section 4 gives experimental results, and Section 5 concludes the paper.
The study uses CORD-19, containing over 45,000 scholarly articles including over 33,000 with full text, and selects 2081 articles and about 360000 sentences published after November 2019.

The authors seek NLP methods to discover unbiased correlation between radiological findings and COVID-19, addressing precise sentence extraction with minimum human annotation and structuring unstructured sentences.
A sentence classifier with bootstrapping and hard examples addresses the first challenge, while constituent parsing and top-frequency noun phrases address the second challenge.
Positive training sentences come from MedPix, which contains more than 9000 topics, 59000 images from 12000 patient cases, while negative sentences are randomly sampled and screened.
The authors train a BERT sentence classifier, pretrain BERT on biomedical literature, add a linear layer, and use the architecture and hyperparameters from BIBREF4.
To reduce false positives, the authors iteratively mine hard examples by labeling top-K sentences with largest prediction scores and retraining the classifier.
The authors use POS tagging and constituent parsing to extract noun phrases containing lesions, abnormalities, diseases, and other important information from unstructured sentences.
Extracted noun phrases have stop words removed, undergo lemmatization, are counted and ranked by frequency, and top-frequency phrases are presented to medical professionals.

The initial classifier used 2350 positive samples from MedPix, 3000 negative samples from CORD-19, 90% training, 10% validation, Adam with learning rate $2\times 10^{-5}$, mini-batch size 4, 400 false positives per iteration, and 4 iterations.

The final classifier predicts 998 positive sentences, with 717 true positives and precision of 71.8%, while the initial classifier achieves precision of 47% and bootstrapping rounds 1-3 achieve 55%, 57%, and 69%.
Table TABREF15 shows top-frequency radiology-relevant noun phrases, with bold phrases such as consolidation, pleural effusion, ground glass opacity, and thickening for further investigation.

Example sentences indicate consolidation is a typical manifestation of COVID-19 and pleural effusion, ground glass opacity, thickening, fibrosis, bronchiectasis, and lymphadenopathy are closely related with COVID-19.
Pleural effusion is supported by BIBREF6: “In terms of pleural changes, CT showed that six (9.7%) had pleural effusion.
Ground glass opacity is supported by BIBREF7: “The predominant pattern of abnormalities after symptom onset was ground-glass opacity (35/78 [45%] to 49/79 [62%] in different periods.
Thickening is supported by BIBREF7 describing ground-glass opacity subcategorized into pure ground-glass opacity and ground-glass opacity with smooth interlobular septal thickening.
Fibrosis is supported by BIBREF8: “In five patients, follow-up CT showed improvement with the appearance of fibrosis and resolution of GGOs.
Bronchiectasis and lymphadenopathy are supported by BIBREF9 listing common and less common chest CT patterns, including bronchiolectasis, pleural effusion, and lymphadenopathy.

The paper develops NLP methods using a BERT-based classifier, bootstrapping, and constituent parsing to extract top-frequency noun phrases and discover COVID-19-related radiological findings from CORD-19.
